server-stateless.rationale: All 27 SEP-2575 checks fail at once ('fetch failed' / 'probe failed completely') because the first harness message kills the child. Root cause, verified against the binary without the bridge: on the stateless wire the harness carries the protocol version in the MCP-Protocol-Version HTTP header and its request _meta contains only io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities and clientInfo, while rmcp 3.0.1's stdio pre-handshake path enters per-request negotiation only when _meta also carries io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion; piping the exact harness-shaped server/discover (clientCapabilities + clientInfo, no protocolVersion) as the first stdio line makes the process print 'MCP initialization failed: expect initialized request, but received: ... DiscoverRequest' and exit, whereas the same message with _meta protocolVersion is answered correctly before any handshake. Two distinct gaps follow: rmcp terminates the stdio connection instead of answering a per-request error for an incompletely negotiated request (an HTTP server answers 400 per request and survives, which is what the sep-2575-request-meta-invalid-* probes expect), and the version-in-header convention has no stdio equivalent the raw bridge could honestly supply. After those are addressed upstream or in the host, roughly half of these checks (every sep-2575-http-server-* one, plus the subscriptions/listen stream group) would still be judging bridge.mjs rather than Bifrost, so this entry is expected to move to a partially-passing state rather than a clean pass; per-check baselining would be the way to close the gap.

caching.rationale: SEP-2549 requires ttlMs and cacheScope on list results at 2026-07-28. Bifrost sets them on tools/list and resources/list (both of those checks pass) but not on prompts/list or resources/templates/list, which rmcp answers with a bare empty list. Failing check ids: sep-2549-prompts-list-caching-hints, sep-2549-resources-templates-list-caching-hints, and wire-schema-valid ('ListPromptsResult: must have required property cacheScope; must have required property ttlMs' for {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"resultType":"complete","prompts":[]}}). This is a genuine wire-schema violation on Bifrost's own bytes: at 2026-07-28 the schema makes those fields required, so any answer Bifrost gives to prompts/list is invalid today. Either add the hints to every list result rmcp can produce, or stop answering methods whose capability Bifrost does not advertise.

input-required-result-unsupported-method.rationale: Its behavioral check passes; the only failure is wire-schema-valid, on the same defect as `caching`: the prompts/list result Bifrost emits at 2026-07-28 omits the required cacheScope and ttlMs ('ListPromptsResult: must have required property cacheScope (result of prompts/list)'). Kept as a second expected failure because it is the narrowest reproduction of that defect and will go green the moment the ListPromptsResult shape is fixed.
